front: Il entra, s'assit et se mit à écrire.
pronunciation: [ee lahn-TRAH, sah-SEE ay suh mee tah ay-KREER]
back: He came in, sat down and began to write.
context: Passé simple: the written narrative tense for completed actions in sequence. Entrer → il entra; s'asseoir → il s'assit; se mettre → il se mit.

front: Ils furent surpris par la nouvelle.
pronunciation: [eel FÜR sür-pree par lah noo-VEL]
back: They were surprised by the news.
context: Passé simple of être: je fus, tu fus, il fut, nous fûmes, vous fûtes, ils furent.

front: Elle naquit à Lyon en 1902.
pronunciation: [el nah-KEE ah lee-OHN ahn meel nuhf-sahn-DUH]
back: She was born in Lyon in 1902.
context: Naître → elle naquit. Common in biographies and encyclopedias.

front: Le roi mourut sans héritier.
pronunciation: [luh RWAH moo-RÜ sahn zay-ree-TYAY]
back: The king died without an heir.
context: Mourir → il mourut.

front: Ils eurent trois enfants.
pronunciation: [eel ZÜR trwah zahn-FAHN]
back: They had three children.
context: Passé simple of avoir: j'eus, tu eus, il eut, nous eûmes, vous eûtes, ils eurent. 'Eu-' is pronounced 'ü'.

front: Il vint, il vit, il vainquit.
pronunciation: [eel VAN, eel VEE, eel van-KEE]
back: He came, he saw, he conquered.
context: Venir → il vint; voir → il vit; vaincre → il vainquit.

front: La lettre que j'ai écrite est partie ce matin.
pronunciation: [lah LET-ruh kuh zhay ay-KREET eh par-TEE suh mah-TAN]
back: The letter I wrote went off this morning.
context: With avoir, the participle agrees with a direct object placed BEFORE it: que (= la lettre) → écrite.

front: Les fleurs que tu m'as offertes sont magnifiques.
pronunciation: [lay FLUHR kuh tü mah zoh-FEHRT sohn mah-nyee-FEEK]
back: The flowers you gave me are magnificent.
context: 'Offertes' agrees with 'que' (= les fleurs, feminine plural). You can hear the t.

front: Ces photos, je les ai prises à Venise.
pronunciation: [say foh-TOH, zhuh lay zay PREEZ ah vuh-NEEZ]
back: These photos, I took them in Venice.
context: 'Les' (= les photos) comes before → prises.

front: Combien de livres as-tu lus cet été ?
pronunciation: [kohm-byan duh LEE-vruh ah-tü LÜ set ay-TAY]
back: How many books did you read this summer?
context: 'Combien de livres' is a direct object before the verb → lus.

front: Des pommes, j'en ai mangé trois.
pronunciation: [day PUM, zhahn nay mahn-zhay TRWAH]
back: Apples, I ate three of them.
context: No agreement with 'en'.

front: Les efforts qu'il a fallu ont été énormes.
pronunciation: [lay zay-FOR keel ah fah-LÜ ohn tay-tay ay-NORM]
back: The efforts that were needed were enormous.
context: Impersonal verbs (falloir, y avoir) never agree.

front: Elles se sont lavées.
pronunciation: [el suh sohn lah-VAY]
back: They washed (themselves).
context: Pronominal verb: 'se' is the direct object → agreement.

front: Elles se sont lavé les mains.
pronunciation: [el suh sohn lah-vay lay MAN]
back: They washed their hands.
context: Here the direct object is 'les mains', after the verb → no agreement.

front: Ils se sont parlé pendant des heures.
pronunciation: [eel suh sohn par-LAY pahn-dahn day ZUHR]
back: They talked to each other for hours.
context: Parler À quelqu'un: 'se' is indirect → no agreement. Same with se sourire, se téléphoner, se succéder.

front: Elle s'est rendu compte de son erreur.
pronunciation: [el seh rahn-dü KOHNT duh soh neh-RUHR]
back: She realized her mistake.
context: 'Se rendre compte': the direct object is 'compte' → 'rendu' never agrees.

front: Je me suis permis de vous écrire.
pronunciation: [zhuh muh swee pehr-MEE duh voo zay-KREER]
back: I took the liberty of writing to you.
context: Permettre À soi → indirect 'se' → no agreement, even for a woman: 'elle s'est permis'.

front: La chanson que j'ai entendu chanter était magnifique.
pronunciation: [lah shahn-SOHN kuh zhay ahn-tahn-dü shahn-TAY ay-teh mah-nyee-FEEK]
back: The song I heard being sung was magnificent.
context: Before an infinitive: no agreement if the object doesn't perform the action (the song isn't singing).

front: La chanteuse que j'ai entendue chanter était magnifique.
pronunciation: [lah shahn-TUHZ kuh zhay ahn-tahn-dü shahn-TAY ay-teh mah-nyee-FEEK]
back: The singer I heard singing was magnificent.
context: Agreement: the singer performs the action.

front: Je crains qu'il ne pleuve.
pronunciation: [zhuh kran keel nuh PLUHV]
back: I'm afraid it may rain.
context: 'Ne explétif': no negative meaning, typical of careful French after verbs of fear.

front: Il est plus intelligent qu'on ne le pense.
pronunciation: [ee leh plü zan-teh-lee-ZHAHN kohn nuh luh PAHNS]
back: He's more intelligent than people think.
context: 'Ne explétif' after unequal comparisons. 'Le' stands for the idea.

front: Il parle bas de peur qu'on ne l'entende.
pronunciation: [eel parl BAH duh puhr kohn nuh lahn-TAHND]
back: He speaks quietly for fear of being overheard.
context: 'De peur que / de crainte que' + subjunctive, often with 'ne'.

front: Je n'ose le lui dire.
pronunciation: [zhuh nohz luh lwee DEER]
back: I daren't tell him.
context: Literary: 'ne' alone (without pas) with oser, pouvoir, savoir and cesser.

front: Il ne cesse de pleuvoir depuis lundi.
pronunciation: [eel nuh ses duh pluh-VWAHR duh-pwee lan-DEE]
back: It hasn't stopped raining since Monday.
context: 'Ne cesser de' = to keep on (formal).

front: Je ne saurais vous dire à quelle heure il arrivera.
pronunciation: [zhuh nuh soh-reh voo DEER ah kel uhr ee lah-reev-RAH]
back: I couldn't tell you what time he'll arrive.
context: 'Je ne saurais' = I couldn't (very polite, formal).

front: Le fait qu'il ait menti me choque.
pronunciation: [luh FEH keel eh mahn-TEE muh SHOK]
back: The fact that he lied shocks me.
context: 'Le fait que' + subjunctive is preferred when the fact is being judged.

front: Que tu sois d'accord ne change rien.
pronunciation: [kuh tü swah dah-KOR nuh shahnzh RYAN]
back: Whether or not you agree changes nothing.
context: A 'que' clause placed first as subject takes the subjunctive.

front: Je comprends qu'il soit déçu.
pronunciation: [zhuh kohm-prahn keel swah day-SÜ]
back: I understand why he's disappointed.
context: 'Comprendre que' = to accept, find normal → subjunctive.

front: J'ai compris qu'il était déçu.
pronunciation: [zhay kohm-pree keel ay-teh day-SÜ]
back: I realized he was disappointed.
context: 'Comprendre que' = to realize → indicative. Same verb, different mood.

front: Il est probable qu'il viendra.
pronunciation: [ee leh proh-BAH-bluh keel vyan-DRAH]
back: He'll probably come.
context: Probability → indicative. But 'il est possible qu'il vienne' (possibility) → subjunctive.

front: Je ne nie pas qu'il ait du talent.
pronunciation: [zhuh nuh NEE pah keel eh dü tah-LAHN]
back: I don't deny he has talent.
context: 'Ne pas nier que' + subjunctive.

front: Si tu viens et que tu as le temps, on ira au musée.
pronunciation: [see tü VYAN ay kuh tü ah luh TAHN, ohn nee-rah oh mü-ZAY]
back: If you come and you have time, we'll go to the museum.
context: 'Que' replaces a second 'si' and keeps the indicative.

front: Quand bien même il s'excuserait, je ne lui pardonnerais pas.
pronunciation: [kahn byan MEM eel sek-skü-zuh-REH, zhuh nuh lwee par-dun-REH PAH]
back: Even if he apologized, I wouldn't forgive him.
context: 'Quand bien même' + conditional = even if.

front: Pour peu qu'il fasse beau, nous sortirons.
pronunciation: [poor PUH keel fas BOH, noo sor-tee-ROHN]
back: If the weather is at all nice, we'll go out.
context: 'Pour peu que' + subjunctive = if only, provided that.

front: Dût-il en souffrir, il dira la vérité.
pronunciation: [dü-TEEL ahn soo-FREER, eel dee-rah lah vay-ree-TAY]
back: Even if he has to suffer for it, he'll tell the truth.
context: Literary: inverted imperfect subjunctive of devoir = even if.

front: Encore faut-il le vouloir.
pronunciation: [ahn-kor foh-TEEL luh voo-LWAHR]
back: You still have to want it, though.
context: 'Encore' at the start means 'still, yet' and triggers inversion.

front: Elle était tout émue.
pronunciation: [el ay-teh too tay-MÜ]
back: She was deeply moved.
context: 'Tout' as an adverb (= very) stays invariable before a vowel or silent h. Compare 'elle était toute honteuse'.

front: Elle était toute honteuse.
pronunciation: [el ay-teh toot ohn-TUHZ]
back: She was very ashamed.
context: Adverb 'tout' agrees before a feminine adjective starting with a consonant or aspirated h. Compare 'elle était tout émue'.

front: Il y a quelque vingt ans, tout était différent.
pronunciation: [eel yah kel-kuh van TAHN, too tay-teh dee-fay-RAHN]
back: Some twenty years ago, everything was different.
context: 'Quelque' before a number = approximately (invariable adverb).

front: Je leur ai rendu leurs clés.
pronunciation: [zhuh luhr ay rahn-dü luhr KLAY]
back: I gave them back their keys.
context: 'Leur' pronoun (to them) never takes s; 'leurs' possessive agrees.

front: Plutôt mourir que céder !
pronunciation: [plü-toh moo-REER kuh say-DAY]
back: I'd rather die than give in!
context: 'Plutôt' = rather; 'plus tôt' = earlier.

front: Il faudrait travailler davantage.
pronunciation: [eel foh-dreh trah-vah-yay dah-vahn-TAHZH]
back: We ought to work more.
context: 'Davantage' = more (elegant alternative to 'plus').

front: Nul n'est censé ignorer la loi.
pronunciation: [NÜL neh sahn-say een-yoh-ray lah LWAH]
back: Ignorance of the law is no excuse.
context: 'Nul' = no one (formal). A legal maxim.

front: Il s'en est fallu de peu qu'on rate le train.
pronunciation: [eel sahn neh fah-lü duh PUH kohn rat luh TRAN]
back: We very nearly missed the train.
context: 'Il s'en est fallu de peu' + subjunctive = it came close.

front: C'est en lisant qu'on apprend à écrire.
pronunciation: [seh tahn lee-ZAHN kohn nah-prahn ah ay-KREER]
back: It's by reading that you learn to write.
context: Gerund: en + present participle, expressing means.

front: Les élèves ayant terminé peuvent sortir.
pronunciation: [lay zay-lev eh-yahn tehr-mee-NAY puhv sor-TEER]
back: Students who have finished may leave.
context: The present participle 'ayant terminé' replaces 'qui ont terminé' (formal).

front: Il est midi et demi.
pronunciation: [ee leh mee-DEE ay duh-MEE]
back: It's half past twelve.
context: 'Demi' after the noun agrees in gender: 'une heure et demie'. Before it, invariable: 'une demi-heure'.

front: Je ne doute pas qu'il réussisse.
pronunciation: [zhuh nuh doot PAH keel ray-ü-SEES]
back: I have no doubt he'll succeed.
context: 'Ne pas douter que' traditionally takes the subjunctive (sometimes with 'ne').

front: Je cherche une maison qui ait un grand jardin.
pronunciation: [zhuh shersh ün meh-ZOHN kee eh tan grahn zhar-DAN]
back: I'm looking for a house that has a big garden.
context: Subjunctive: the house is hypothetical. 'Une maison qui a un grand jardin' = a specific one you know exists.

front: Après que vous aurez signé, nous vous enverrons une copie.
pronunciation: [ah-preh kuh voo zoh-ray see-NYAY, noo voo zahn-veh-rohn zün koh-PEE]
back: Once you've signed, we'll send you a copy.
context: Future perfect after 'après que' for a future sequence. Indicative, not subjunctive.
